ME-32: a single bounded adjacent-joint degenerative association has been authored from post-traumatic ankle-degeneration clinical evidence; the draft-safe association stands until qualified-human review.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-32 adds this relationship only as a bounded adjacent-joint degenerative association. Joint ankylosis alters segmental motion and load transfer, and post-traumatic ankle-degeneration literature documents progressive arthritic change in and around stiffened or fused joints, but the primary diagnosis alone does not establish adjacent-segment osteoarthritis in every person or determine an individual's degenerative course. Require independently documented ankylosis of the affected joint by clinical and imaging assessment, radiographically documented adjacent or ipsilateral-segment osteoarthritis compatible in chronology, and orthopedic review. Preserve prior fracture, inflammatory arthropathy, surgical fusion, infection, and primary degenerative disease as competing causes.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of the ankylosed joint by clinical and imaging assessment
Radiographic documentation of adjacent-segment or ipsilateral osteoarthritis with compatible chronology
Assessment of prior fracture, fusion surgery, and infection history
Assessment of inflammatory arthropathy and primary degenerative alternatives
Orthopedic assessment distinguishing ankylosis-related degeneration from other causes

sourceReferences.citation: Krähenbühl N, Susdorf R, Barg A, et al. Supramalleolar osteotomy in post-traumatic valgus ankle osteoarthritis. Int Orthop. 2020;44(3):535-543. PMID 31925464. doi:10.1007/s00264-019-04476-x.
sourceReferences.note: Clinical review of post-traumatic ankle osteoarthritis documenting progressive degenerative change with altered joint mechanics and malalignment. It supports a bounded disease-association proposition and clinical evaluation, not automatic individual causation or aggravation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 31925464; post-traumatic ankle osteoarthritis with altered mechanics and malalignment

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Ankylosis alters joint loading and segmental mechanics, and post-traumatic degeneration literature associates altered joint mechanics with progressive arthritis, but that evidence does not establish an individual medical nexus without documentation of both the ankylosis and the osteoarthritis, compatible chronology, and competing-cause review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by this association evidence; the mapping is not an individual nexus opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Loss of segmental motion from ankylosis redistributes stress to adjacent joints and residual articulations, hypothesized to accelerate cartilage wear, but the individual pathway must be established from serial imaging, alignment assessment, and orthopedic evaluation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Altered joint mechanics from stiffness or fusion are associated with progressive degeneration in orthopedic literature, but that evidence does not establish that ankylosis caused or aggravated osteoarthritis in every individual; both diagnoses, chronology, imaging findings, and competing etiologies require case-specific review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented ankylosis and osteoarthritis; chronology; serial weight-bearing imaging; fracture, surgical, infectious, and inflammatory alternatives; orthopedic assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Prior fracture, surgical fusion, or infectious arthritis of the index joint
Primary osteoarthritis of independent etiology in the adjacent segment
